item.title: Implement retry_budget.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator's words (authenticated chat, local_socket): "Implement `retry_budget.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: make retry_budget.py fully conform to SPEC.md in the repository root.
Acceptance criteria:
- Every API in SPEC.md exists with the documented signature and behaviour; no API removed or renamed.
- Every error case and boundary case named in SPEC.md raises or returns exactly as specified.
- Only the Python standard library is used.
- New focused tests cover each error path and boundary case in SPEC.md, in addition to the existing tests; the full test suite passes.
- Functions stay under 60 lines and follow the repository's existing style; validate inputs at the boundary, do not hide failures.
- Commit the work on the local branch with a clear message. Do not push.
Read SPEC.md first and treat it as the source of truth; if it is ambiguous, pick the most reasonable reading and state the assumption in the commit message.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier

model_reasons.implement: Single small stdlib module plus tests; medium effort suffices.

state.summary:
Implemented retry_delay in retry_budget.py per SPEC.md and added 28 focused tests in test_retry_budget.py, committed as efb9378 on archon/sheqq3x7-implement-retry-budget-py-per-spec-md-wi (not pushed). Validation runs first and raises ValueError for non-int, bool, float or subclass values and for out-of-range values. It then handles the attempt limit, the backoff min(cap, base*2**(attempt-1)) with saturation that avoids large powers, the uncapped retry_after floor, and the strict budget check. Before: the three existing tests errored with NotImplementedError. After: `python3 -I -m unittest` runs 31 tests, all OK, stdlib only. Assumptions (recorded in the commit message): "built-in int" means type(x) is int; a delay ending exactly at budget_ms is refused. Nothing left open; no servers or processes were started. Review: the reviewer returned pass with one non-blocking style nit (_validate_args has no assertions of its own).

pr.body: Approach: _validate_args/_require_int validate every argument at the boundary with ValueError; _backoff saturates via bit_length of cap_ms so huge attempts allocate no large power; retry_delay applies attempt limit, uncapped retry_after floor, and strict budget check. Files: retry_budget.py, test_retry_budget.py. Checks: python3 -I -m unittest -q, 31 tests OK; baseline on 7db56f4 had 3 NotImplementedError errors. Assumptions: type(x) is int (bool, float, None, int subclasses rejected); delay ending exactly at budget_ms is refused. Review: pass, one non-blocking style nit about no asserts in _validate_args.
pr.summary: made retry_budget.retry_delay follow SPEC.md. now validates args, caps backoff, floors retry_after, enforces budget. before: NotImplementedError, now: 31 tests pass.
